label: Vera C. Rubin Observatory (Cerro Pachón)
sub: 8.4m Simonyi Survey Telescope with the 3,200-megapixel LSST Camera; summit elevation ~2,647m

label: Rubin Auxiliary Telescope
sub: 1.2m calibration telescope on the Cerro Pachón summit used for atmospheric monitoring supporting the main survey

label: Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory
sub: NOIRLab's original Chile flagship site, about 10km northeast of Cerro Pachón, hosts the Blanco 4m telescope and DECam

label: Gemini South Telescope
sub: 8.1m telescope sharing the Cerro Pachón ridge with Rubin Observatory

label: SOAR Telescope
sub: 4.1m Southern Astrophysical Research Telescope on the Cerro Pachón ridge

label: AURA Recinto / NOIRLab Chile Headquarters, La Serena
sub: Administrative and logistics hub supporting Rubin, Cerro Tololo, and Gemini South operations

label: Rubin Observatory Base Facility
sub: Remote-operations and data-processing support base near La Serena

label: Vicuña
sub: Nearest town to Cerro Pachón and Cerro Tololo; Elqui Valley dark-sky tourism hub

label: La Florida Airport, La Serena
sub: Nearest commercial airport for observatory staff and visitor transit

label: Port of Coquimbo
sub: Regional port used for heavy freight, including telescope and camera components shipped from the United States

label: Cerro Pachón Access Road
sub: Mountain access route connecting the summit facilities to Route 41 and La Serena

label: Elqui Valley International Dark Sky Sanctuary
sub: World's first International Dark Sky Sanctuary, protecting the night skies used by Rubin and neighboring observatories

label: 'First Stone' Ceremony Site
sub: April 14, 2015 — Cerro Pachón groundbreaking attended by President Bachelet and NSF Director France Córdova

label: Simonyi Survey Telescope Dedication Site
sub: October 4, 2024 — ceremony naming the 8.4m telescope for donor Charles Simonyi

label: 'First Photon' Commissioning Site
sub: October 24, 2024 — the Commissioning Camera captured the telescope's first on-sky images
